message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "Massive left pleural effusion", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates complete opacification (white-out) of the left hemithorax with a contralateral mediastinal shift to the right. According to skill t000003, this specific combination of unilateral white-out and push-effect shift is the hallmark radiological sign of a massive pleural effusion. In contrast, lung collapse (Option A) would typically cause an ipsilateral shift (pull effect), and pneumonia (Options C, F) usually preserves volume or causes minimal shift without significant mass effect. Tension pneumothorax (Option D) would present as hyperlucency (black), not opacity. Although the classifier only flagged 'Lung Opacity' and the report generator was limited by habitus, the visual morphology of space-occupying fluid displacing the mediastinum strongly supports massive effusion over other differentials."}
